decisions.decision: One Python codebase, feature-sliced, run as 3 processes (api / grpc / worker). Described honestly as one platform service with bounded contexts, not as 3 microservices. Design doc shows the production split (payments-ledger, fraud, support-ai).
decisions.why: Ledger atomicity stays in one DB transaction; demo reliability; all 13 Basic items first.

decisions.decision: Deterministic tools compute facts and money; LLM parses NL into typed filters, picks tools, and narrates. Settlement narration is generated from a verified typed breakdown.
decisions.why: Numbers must never be invented; also gives an evaluable boundary.

decisions.decision: Postgres unique (merchant_id, idempotency_key) + request hash as source of truth; stored response replayed; Redis is only a fast path.
decisions.why: Redis loss must not allow a double charge.

decisions.decision: Transactional outbox in the payment DB transaction -> relay -> Redis Streams -> consumers with dedupe by event id.
decisions.why: Without it a crash between commit and publish loses confirmations and fraud alerts (raised by Sol).

decisions.decision: Both API validation (Pydantic / protobuf + business rules) and AI guardrails (tenant scope from auth only, tool allowlist + typed args, retrieved text untrusted, abstain on weak evidence).
decisions.why: The brief's wording is ambiguous; covering both is safer for a 'missing item = fail' rule.

decisions.decision: Redis session (TTL, merchant-isolated) + last N turns + structured conversation state; long-term = explicit auditable merchant_memory written only via confirmed tool call, with source turn id, correct/delete. No silent LLM fact extraction.
decisions.why: Interview weak spot; must be demonstrable and auditable without false-memory risk.

decisions.decision: Primary: live burst through the merchant API on a fixed fixture; fallback: seeded dataset burst.
decisions.why: Shows sync + async pipeline end to end.

decisions.decision: Ground truth from planted scenarios, but questions written independently of generator templates (paraphrases, compound conditions, no-answer, cross-merchant probes). Separate metrics for retrieval, tool choice/args, and answer grounding; keyword vs vector vs hybrid ablation. Deterministic metrics in CI; DeepEval LLM metrics only with a real key.
decisions.why: Avoid a circular RAG evaluation story.

decisions.decision: Merchant API keys stored hashed; users use session tokens after password + TOTP.
decisions.why: Separate B2B and B2C auth paths.

decisions.topic: Product purpose, users, mandatory capabilities, scope
decisions.decision: Purpose: safe and reliable payments; when a payment fails, is declined, looks fraudulent or settles differently than expected, merchants and operations staff decide cause and response with evidence and act within safe limits. Primary users: merchants and operations staff; consumers use payment functions; financial institutions are counterparties. Mandatory = the 13 Basic items only, in 6 groups (payment core B1-B3, merchant integration B8, risk B7, operations intelligence B4-B6/B9/B10, operations workflow B11-B12, interfaces B13). Ledger / zero double charge / card-testing detection are kept as design choices or verification scenarios, not requirements. No real money movement; Advanced and NFRs are not part of the purpose; scale/compliance reported as demonstrated vs production-design-only.
decisions.why: The Overview's last sentence is a capability list, not a purpose; it drops the problem (failures, fraud, settlement) and the users the sample queries come from.

decision.thesis: Explain payment outcomes with evidence, and guide the next safe step.
decision.entry_points: A question (primary; all 4 sample queries) or an alert (secondary; shown with card testing), both into one investigation flow. Proactive failure-rate anomaly detection kept light (not Basic).
decision.loop: Investigate (ranked hypotheses with evidence, data-as-of, gaps; SQ1 also shows alternative hypotheses and when NOT to reroute) -> Respond (approved routing override, or ticket/notification with evidence pack) -> Verify (time-ordered replay; 'recovery observed', never 'effect proven') -> Learn (AI layer only; human verdicts go to a separate feedback set; golden eval set stays frozen).
decision.routing_override_safety: Applied conditionally on config version + operation id; TTL expiry reverts only if the config is still at the version it set.
decision.tiers: Failure-behavior classification, not an availability guarantee. T0 must not stop: gateway sync path, no LLM. T1 may delay, must not lose: outbox (retained, replayable) / stream / settlement / notifications, plus AI-layer deterministic parts (projections rebuildable from Postgres, alert rules, ticket routing) that work without an LLM. T2 may degrade: LLM diagnosis/assistant falls back to dashboards + evidence list with retrieval time (no NL fallback).
decision.authorization: Tenant and role checked at every stage (retrieval, history, tool call); instructions inside merchant documents never grant permissions.
decision.claims: Every tier/region claim labeled demonstrated vs production-design-only. Data residency claim covers the LLM provider: prompts minimized, provider regional terms verified before any claim.
decision.unchanged: Stablecoin not the core (design-only rail at most). Home region per account, production design only; AI projections in the same home region.
decision.design_doc: Keeps a Basic 13-item mapping so payment features are not hidden behind the AI story.

decisions.why: Align with D-012/D-013; critical review found the push-first loop, action-centric thesis, unsupported 'no loss' claim, eval contamination and override conflicts.
still_deferred: Agent framework incl. OpenAI Agents SDK

decisions.decision: Narrate as a payment-operations AI layer that attaches to any gateway through an event and tool boundary (B); satisfy Basic by also implementing the gateway as the reference implementation (A).
decisions.why: Matches the FDE job (add AI on top of a customer's existing system); Basic still requires the payment core.

decisions.decision: Ops port = 3 contracts, every one carrying merchant scope taken from caller auth (never from LLM args). (1) Events in via outbox: payment outcomes (raw provider code + normalized code + mapping version, 'unclassified' allowed; retry eligibility not normalized), provider health, risk flags, settlement/payout breakdowns, config/routing/rule/deploy changes; each with event id, schema version, occurred_at, entity version; token id + BIN/last4 only, no PAN, minimal PII. (2) Reads: thin AI-side projections (search documents, investigation aggregates; no ledger/balance copies); authoritative point lookups via gateway query API; answers state data-as-of time and gaps; time coincidence with a change is a hypothesis, not a cause. (3) Commands: one only - routing override for new payments, scoped to a route, with TTL; approval token bound to operation, target, tenant, expiry; gateway re-validates current state and permission at execution. Other responses go to humans via tickets/notifications. Never: vault/PAN, ledger writes, sync auth path, fraud rules. Card testing: real-time detection/blocking = gateway; delayed detection, investigation, alerts = AI layer. Transactional notifications = gateway; alerts and tickets = AI layer, both deduped. Normalized taxonomy belongs to the port; adapters normalize. Adapter capabilities filter the tools exposed to the LLM. No AI-to-gateway learning channel for now. One codebase; boundary enforced by an import-rule test.
decisions.why: Positioning B needs a real, enforced boundary; panel will attack stale-observation actions, so the gateway is the enforcement point.
decisions.supersedes: Earlier stance that AI may propose retrying definitive failures (removed).

open_questions.question: OK to ship one platform service run as api/grpc/worker processes (D-001) instead of several independent microservices?

Stack addition: for no-key mode, bundle a pinned small local embedding model (e.g. fastembed ONNX bge-small, ~130MB, baked into the image) instead of a hashing embedder? Alternatives: hashing embedder (weak semantics), or require an OpenAI key for the demo.
open_questions.answer: Use a pinned local embedding model (fastembed bge-small, ~130MB, baked into the image) in no-key mode; OpenAI embeddings when a key is present.

open_questions.question: Demo clock: the brief says 'this afternoon'. Use an injectable clock with a fixed DEMO_NOW + timezone shown in the UI (reproducible), with the dataset anchored to it? Or anchor to the real current date?
Project-level dependencies: Python via uv (pyproject + lock) and frontend via npm (package-lock), inside Docker and under nix shell locally. No global installs. Acceptable under the 'Nix only' rule?
open_questions.answer: uv (pyproject + lock) and npm (package-lock), project-local only, used inside Docker and nix shell; no global installs. Reviewers need Docker only.

open_questions.question: OpenAI default model names for .env.example (chat, embedding, judge)? Will you provide an OPENAI_API_KEY for the demo and DeepEval runs (cost)?
open_questions.default_if_no_answer: Placeholders in .env.example; mock everywhere until a key is provided.
